newsitem.title: USA: Holbrooke to join U.S. mission to Balkans.
newsitem.headline: Holbrooke to join U.S. mission to Balkans.

text.p: Former Bosnia peace negotiator Richard Holbrooke will revisit the Balkans next week as part of a U.S. team that will press for implementation of the Dayton peace accords, the State Department said on Wednesday.
Spokesman James Foley said the delegation would be led by Robert Gelbard, U.S. special representative for Dayton implementation, and would visit Bosnia, Serbia and Croatia.

He said the mission would discuss U.S. concerns about implementation of the accords, which were reached in November 1995 largely thanks to the efforts of Holbrooke, who was an assistant secretary of state at the time.

Foley said the team, expected to include State Department, Pentagon and National Security Council officials, would travel to the region on or about Aug. 6 and meet key Balkan leaders, including all parties to the Dayton accords.
The itinerary was not complete, he added.

The team will press for "concrete action" on the accords, which while they ended Bosnia's civil war have failed to lead to the handover of most war criminals, the return of most refugees to their homes, or ethnic reconciliation.
Dayton provided for a single Bosnian state divided into a Serb republic and a Moslem-Croat federation. Getting the two entities to cooperate has proved an uphill struggle.
Holbrooke, whose tough style of negotiating was respected by friend and foe alike, quit government service in February 1996 to join Credit Suisse First Boston bank, a position he still holds.
He was recently appointed a part-time U.S. envoy on the Cyprus problem.
The aim of sending the team to Bosnia "clearly is to send a very strong signal to the parties of our very strong expectation that they get with it on Dayton implementation," Foley said.

He said it was Gelbard's idea to invite Holbrooke along. "Obviously, Ambassador Holbrooke has a record of success and I think it's a very positive thing that Ambassador Holbrooke is willing to take up his personal time to go along with Ambassador Gelbard on the visit," he said.
